name: Smothered Beefsteak
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: thin slices of steak from the upper part of the round or one large thin steak
ingredients.originalText: thin slices of steak from the upper part of the round or one large thin steak

ingredients.name: powdered summer savory
ingredients.originalText: half a teaspoonful powdered summer savory

instructions.text: Lay the meat out smoothly and wipe it dry
Prepare a dressing using bread crumbs, salt, pepper, butter, sage, powdered summer savory, and enough milk to moisten into a stiff mixture
Spread the dressing over the meat
Roll it up carefully and tie with a string, securing the ends well
Fry a few thin slices of salt pork in the bottom of a kettle or saucepan
Place the roll or rolls of beef into the fat and brown on all sides, turning until a rich color all over
Add half a pint of water
If desired, chop a slice of onion fine and add to the dressing
When cooked sufficiently, take out the meat and thicken the gravy
Turn the gravy over the meat
Carve by cutting crosswise in slices through beef and stuffing

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Lay the meat out smoothly and wipe it dry
2. Prepare a dressing using bread crumbs, salt, pepper, butter, sage, powdered summer savory, and enough milk to moisten into a stiff mixture
3. Spread the dressing over the meat
4. Roll it up carefully and tie with a string, securing the ends well
5. Fry a few thin slices of salt pork in the bottom of a kettle or saucepan
6. Place the roll or rolls of beef into the fat and brown on all sides, turning until a rich color all over
7. Add half a pint of water
8. Stew until tender
9. If desired, chop a slice of onion fine and add to the dressing
10. When cooked sufficiently, take out the meat and thicken the gravy
11. Turn the gravy over the meat
12. Carve by cutting crosswise in slices through beef and stuffing
